course_title: Practical Exercise on European and Global Legal History
title: Exercise class 2: ancient cultures, Jewish and Islamic law

slides.title: The Romans, the Greeks and what each left behind
slides.text: The exercise class's answer to the question whether the Romans 'invented' law is NO — and it adds at once where the merit lies. THERE WERE ANCIENT NON-WESTERN LEGAL CULTURES long before. WHAT THE ROMANS ACTUALLY CREATED IS A NORMATIVE LEGAL SYSTEM, ESPECIALLY IN THE FIELD OF CIVIL LAW, WHICH TO THIS DAY FORMS THE BASIS OF CONTINENTAL EUROPEAN LEGAL CULTURE. THE GREEKS DID NOT YET HAVE SO DEVELOPED A SYSTEM, not least BECAUSE THEY HAD MANY SEPARATE CITY STATES — the law was fragmented and had nowhere to unify. And the exercise adds an observation worth remembering: FOR THE GREEKS LAW WAS ABOVE ALL PART OF RHETORIC, the art of persuading an assembly or a jury, not a specialist discipline of concepts. THEIR INFLUENCE LIES MAINLY IN LEGAL PHILOSOPHY — in the SOPHISTS, PLATO and ARISTOTLE.

cards.q: What did the Romans create and why did the Greeks not?
cards.a: The Romans created a NORMATIVE LEGAL SYSTEM, especially in CIVIL LAW, which to this day forms the basis of continental European legal culture. The Greeks had no such developed system, not least BECAUSE THEY HAD MANY SEPARATE CITY STATES. And FOR THE GREEKS LAW WAS ABOVE ALL PART OF RHETORIC, not a specialist discipline — their influence lies in LEGAL PHILOSOPHY.

slides.title: The Sophists: man the measure of all things
slides.text: FROM THE 5TH CENTURY BC THE SOPHISTS QUESTIONED THAT LAW IS GIVEN BY THE GODS AND THEREFORE BINDING ON ALL LIVING BEINGS — and the exercise class expressly adds that there are PARALLELS WITH THE ENLIGHTENMENT, that is, that this is the same type of questioning of authority two thousand years earlier. PROTAGORAS doubted the very existence of the gods, and for him MAN BECAME 'THE MEASURE OF ALL THINGS'. From this follows a question that has never gone away: MUST LAW BE JUST, AND WHOSE JUSTICE MUST IT MATCH — DIVINE OR HUMAN? The Sophists therefore began to distinguish between RECORDED LAW (later to be called POSITIVE) and LAW THAT IS VALID BY NATURE, INDEPENDENTLY OF ALL POSITIVE LAW — that is, NOMOS AGAINST PHYSIS. SOCRATES, and after him PLATO and ARISTOTLE, then concerned themselves above all with ETHICS as a counterweight to this relativism. CICERO summed it up in a sentence worth knowing in Latin: 'LEX EST RATIO SUMMA INSITA IN NATURA' — law is the highest reason implanted in nature. AND THE CONSEQUENCE THE EXERCISE DRAWS FROM IT IS HARSH: A POSITIVE STATUTE THAT CONTRADICTS NATURAL LAW IS NULL AND VOID — IT DOES NOT BIND.

terms.term: lex est ratio summa insita in natura
terms.def: Law is the highest reason implanted in nature (Cicero) — the basis of the argument that a contradicting positive statute does not bind.

cards.q: What did the Sophists question, and what distinction did that lead to?
cards.a: From the 5th century BC they questioned THAT LAW IS GIVEN BY THE GODS and therefore binding on all (A PARALLEL WITH THE ENLIGHTENMENT). PROTAGORAS doubted the existence of the gods and for him MAN BECAME 'THE MEASURE OF ALL THINGS'. It led to the distinction between RECORDED LAW (later positive) and LAW VALID BY NATURE — NOMOS against PHYSIS.
cards.topic: Ancient Legal Cultures; History of Islamic Law

cards.q: Quote Cicero on law and say what follows from it.
cards.a: 'LEX EST RATIO SUMMA INSITA IN NATURA' — law is THE HIGHEST REASON IMPLANTED IN NATURE. It follows that A POSITIVE STATUTE CONTRADICTING NATURAL LAW IS NULL AND VOID — IT DOES NOT BIND.

slides.title: From the Neolithic to the first written law
slides.text: The exercise class gives the development in stages, and it is a neat answer to the question WHY there of all places. THE NEOLITHIC — PROPERTY ALREADY IMPLIES LAW: where wealth accumulates, it must be settled to whom it belongs. THE 6TH MILLENNIUM BC — everything appears at once: HIERARCHIZATION, STANDARDIZED MEASURES, THE FIRST SETTLEMENTS, INSTRUMENTS OF ADMINISTRATION, THE FIRST EVIDENCE OF MASSACRES AND WAR, NAME SEALS, SURPLUS AND CENTRAL PLANNING, UNIFICATION. THE 3RD MILLENNIUM BC — an ADVANCED CIVILIZATION with WRITING and a CALENDAR in the territory of today's Syria, Iraq and Iran. MESOPOTAMIA specifically: MANY CITY STATES, THE FIRST WRITTEN LAW (on the administration of goods and on contracts — divorce, inheritance, adoption, slavery) and MAINTAINED RELATIONS WITH THE OTHER CITY STATES. And from that last point follows the most interesting thing: TWO TREATIES FROM THE 3RD MILLENNIUM BC have survived — the STELE OF THE VULTURES and the PEACE TREATY BETWEEN EBLA AND ABARSAL. They are therefore THE OLDEST EVIDENCE OF SOMETHING ONE MIGHT CALL INTERNATIONAL LAW.

cards.q: What appears in the 6th millennium BC and why does it concern law?
cards.a: HIERARCHIZATION, STANDARDIZED MEASURES, THE FIRST SETTLEMENTS, INSTRUMENTS OF ADMINISTRATION, THE FIRST EVIDENCE OF MASSACRES AND WAR, NAME SEALS, SURPLUS AND CENTRAL PLANNING, UNIFICATION. Already in the NEOLITHIC, PROPERTY IMPLIES LAW — where wealth accumulates, it must be settled to whom it belongs.
cards.topic: Ancient Legal Cultures; History of Islamic Law

cards.q: Which two treaties from the 3rd millennium BC survive, and why do they matter?
cards.a: The STELE OF THE VULTURES and the PEACE TREATY BETWEEN EBLA AND ABARSAL. They matter because they are THE OLDEST EVIDENCE OF SOMETHING ONE MIGHT CALL INTERNATIONAL LAW — the Mesopotamian city states maintained relations with one another.

slides.title: The Stele of the Vultures
slides.text: THE STELE OF THE VULTURES is the OLDEST KNOWN WAR MONUMENT and comes from the EARLY DYNASTIC IIIb PERIOD (2600–2350 BC) in Mesopotamia. It celebrates the VICTORY OF THE CITY STATE OF LAGASH OVER NEIGHBOURING UMMA. The fragments were found in southern Iraq at the end of the 19th century and are today in the LOUVRE. From the inscriptions we know that the stele was commissioned by EANNATUM, the ENSI or ruler of Lagash, around 2460 BC; on it he describes the DISPUTE WITH UMMA OVER GU-EDIN, a strip of agricultural land lying between the two city states. The dispute ends in a battle in which Eannatum — described as the beloved of the god Ningirsu — defeats Umma. AND NOW THE LEGALLY INTERESTING PART: AFTER THE BATTLE THE LEADER OF UMMA SWEARS NEVER AGAIN TO CROSS THE TERRITORY OF LAGASH, ON PAIN OF PUNISHMENT. So we have a border dispute, its resolution by force, and finally AN OBLIGATION CONFIRMED BY OATH AND SECURED BY A SANCTION — that is, all the elements of an interstate treaty, four and a half thousand years before the Peace of Westphalia.

cards.q: What is the Stele of the Vultures and why is it legally interesting?
cards.a: The OLDEST KNOWN WAR MONUMENT (Early Dynastic IIIb, 2600–2350 BC), celebrating the victory of LAGASH OVER UMMA; commissioned by EANNATUM around 2460 BC, today in the LOUVRE. It describes the DISPUTE OVER GU-EDIN, a strip of agricultural land between the two states — and after the battle THE LEADER OF UMMA SWEARS NOT TO CROSS THE TERRITORY OF LAGASH AGAIN, ON PAIN OF PUNISHMENT. All the elements of an interstate treaty are there.

slides.title: Egypt and Mesopotamia: continuity against alternation
slides.text: The exercise class sets the two empires against each other, and the contrast makes a good answer. EGYPT: the UNIFICATION OF UPPER AND LOWER EGYPT BY KING MENES (32nd century BC); a LONG AND CONTINUOUS DEVELOPMENT OF THE STATE with three periods of flowering (the OLD, MIDDLE AND NEW KINGDOMS) interspersed with intermediate periods; IN 343 BC it becomes part of the Persian empire. EGYPTIAN LAW is attested by a GREAT NUMBER OF WILLS, CONTRACTS, ADOPTIONS AND OTHER LEGAL TRANSACTIONS — preserved on PAPYRI (the Vienna Papyrusmuseum has one of the largest collections in the world). MESOPOTAMIA, by contrast, HAS NO CONTINUOUS DEVELOPMENT: empires form ALTERNATELY IN THE NORTH (ASSYRIA) AND IN THE SOUTH (BABYLONIA), and in 539 BC the whole region becomes part of the Persian empire. MESOPOTAMIAN LAW has SEVERAL LEGAL RECORDS — THE OLDEST IS THE CODE OF UR-NAMMU (23rd/21st century BC), THE MOST FAMOUS THAT OF HAMMURABI (18th century BC). And the exercise expressly opens a dispute that has no clear answer: THE NATURE OF THOSE RECORDS IS DEBATABLE — is it STATUTORY LAW, or a RECORD OF CUSTOMARY LAW? That is: did the ruler lay down new norms, or merely write down what was being observed anyway?

cards.q: Compare the development of the state in Egypt and Mesopotamia.
cards.a: EGYPT: the UNIFICATION OF UPPER AND LOWER EGYPT BY KING MENES (32nd c. BC), a LONG AND CONTINUOUS DEVELOPMENT with the Old, Middle and New Kingdoms; in 343 BC part of the Persian empire. MESOPOTAMIA: NO CONTINUOUS DEVELOPMENT — empires form ALTERNATELY IN THE NORTH (Assyria) AND THE SOUTH (Babylonia); in 539 BC part of the Persian empire.
cards.topic: Ancient Legal Cultures; History of Islamic Law

cards.q: What dispute about the nature of the Mesopotamian codes does the exercise open?
cards.a: Whether it is STATUTORY LAW or a RECORD OF CUSTOMARY LAW — that is, whether the ruler laid down new norms or merely wrote down what was observed anyway. The answer is not clear. (The oldest record is the CODE OF UR-NAMMU, the most famous that of HAMMURABI.)

slides.title: Why Jewish law is 'governed by people' — the exercise's answer
slides.text: The exercise class gives four points in answer to this question, and all of them are COMPARATIVE, that is, defined against the Western ideal — which is precisely what makes them a good answer. (1) UNLIKE THE WESTERN IDEAL, JUDGES MAY DEPART FROM THE RULE. Where for us a departure from the norm is a defect, there it is part of the judicial role. (2) THERE ARE NO EQUITY COURTS — because there is no need for a second system to mitigate the harshness of the rule; that function is performed by the judge himself within a single system. (3) THERE IS NO APPELLATE COURT. (4) THERE IS NO DOCTRINE OF BINDING PRECEDENT. (5) And the summary, to be remembered verbatim: THE JUDGE IS A SPIRITUAL LEADER AND A MODEL, NOT A TECHNOCRAT. From those points the explanation also follows: where law has no state to enforce it, it is held together by the AUTHORITY OF THE PERSON, not by a hierarchy of institutions — and correspondingly it is not checked by appeal but by the standing of the scholar. A NOTE ON THE DIASPORA: the exercise dates it FROM THE BABYLONIAN CAPTIVITY (around 600 BC), and its legal consequence is THE EMERGENCE OF A LEGAL SYSTEM (HALAKHA) DETACHED FROM ANY PARTICULAR TERRITORY. THE SOURCES: the TORAH (the Old Testament) and the TALMUD — the JERUSALEM Talmud around AD 400, the BABYLONIAN around AD 600; the Talmud has two parts, the MISHNAH (the written summary of the oral Torah) and the GEMARA (the commentary).

cards.q: How does the exercise answer the question why Jewish law is 'governed by people, not by rules'?
cards.a: By four comparative points: 1) UNLIKE THE WESTERN IDEAL, JUDGES MAY DEPART FROM THE RULE. 2) THERE ARE NO EQUITY COURTS. 3) THERE IS NO APPELLATE COURT. 4) THERE IS NO DOCTRINE OF BINDING PRECEDENT. And the summary: THE JUDGE IS A SPIRITUAL LEADER AND A MODEL, NOT A TECHNOCRAT.

cards.q: From when is the diaspora counted, and how are the two Talmuds dated?
cards.a: From the BABYLONIAN CAPTIVITY, around 600 BC; its legal consequence is THE EMERGENCE OF HALAKHA AS A SYSTEM DETACHED FROM TERRITORY. The JERUSALEM TALMUD around AD 400, the BABYLONIAN around AD 600; both have the MISHNAH (the written summary of the oral Torah) and the GEMARA (the commentary).

slides.title: From Muhammad to Sunnis and Shiites
slides.text: MUHAMMAD (between AD 570 and 632) founded the Islamic religion on the ARABIAN PENINSULA. The period before him is called the JAHILIYYA — the 'age of ignorance', the dark age. AFTER MUHAMMAD'S DEATH A STRUGGLE OVER THE SUCCESSION BROKE OUT and IN 656 THE SCHISM OCCURRED: the governor of SYRIA founded the UMAYYAD DYNASTY and the CALIPHS — that is, SPIRITUAL AND TEMPORAL LEADERS IN ONE PERSON — ruled from DAMASCUS; from this branch comes SUNNI ISLAM, today the largest branch. THE GEOGRAPHY OF THE CALIPHATE: the caliphs ruled from DAMASCUS (to 749), then from BAGHDAD (to the Mongol invasion) and from the 13th century until 1517 from CAIRO, over an empire reaching FROM SPAIN TO CENTRAL ASIA. AL-ANDALUS is the Muslim-ruled part of the Iberian peninsula FROM THE 8TH CENTURY UNTIL 1492 (the Reconquista). IN 1517 THE OTTOMANS CONQUERED EGYPT and THE OTTOMAN SULTANS THEREAFTER CLAIMED THE TITLE OF CALIPH — UNTIL THE ABOLITION OF THE SULTANATE IN 1922. THE SHIITES: at the schism in the 7th century a smaller part remained loyal to MUHAMMAD'S GRANDSON and venerates him and his descendants as IMAMS. Hence the Shiites, for example in IRAN, where the idea of the RETURN OF THE MAHDI persists to this day — and the exercise adds a constitutional consequence worth remembering: UNDER THE CONSTITUTION OF THE IRANIAN REPUBLIC OF 1979, THE RULE OF THE SUPREME JURISTS IS ONLY VICARIOUS UNTIL THE MAHDI RETURNS. The supreme cleric therefore does not rule in his own right but on behalf of the absent one.

terms.def: The 'age of ignorance' — the name for the period on the Arabian peninsula before Muhammad.

cards.q: How and when did the schism between Sunnis and Shiites occur?
cards.a: After Muhammad's death (632) a STRUGGLE OVER THE SUCCESSION broke out and IN 656 THE SCHISM OCCURRED: the governor of SYRIA founded the UMAYYAD DYNASTY and the caliphs ruled from DAMASCUS — hence SUNNI ISLAM. A smaller part remained loyal to MUHAMMAD'S GRANDSON and venerates his descendants as IMAMS — hence the SHIITES.

cards.q: From where did the caliphs rule and when did the title disappear?
cards.a: From DAMASCUS (to 749), then from BAGHDAD (to the Mongol invasion) and from the 13th century until 1517 from CAIRO, over an empire FROM SPAIN TO CENTRAL ASIA. IN 1517 THE OTTOMANS CONQUERED EGYPT and the Ottoman sultans claimed the title of caliph UNTIL THE ABOLITION OF THE SULTANATE IN 1922. AL-ANDALUS lasted from the 8th century UNTIL 1492.

cards.q: What constitutional consequence does the expectation of the Mahdi have in Iran?
cards.a: UNDER THE CONSTITUTION OF THE IRANIAN REPUBLIC OF 1979, THE RULE OF THE SUPREME JURISTS IS ONLY VICARIOUS UNTIL THE MAHDI RETURNS — the supreme cleric therefore does not rule in his own right but ON BEHALF OF THE ABSENT ONE.

slides.title: Sharia and fiqh: what is divided and what is not
slides.text: To sharia the exercise class adds three distinctions that are not found elsewhere. (1) SHARIA IS INSEPARABLE FROM ISLAM; the central source is the QUR'AN as the LITERAL REVELATION OF GOD to the Prophet, the further ones being the SUNNA (attested by hadith), IJMA (the consensus of the scholars) and, among the Shiites, the NORMATIVE PRACTICE OF THE IMAMS. (2) FIQH, that is, LEGAL SCIENCE, ESTABLISHED ITSELF AS AN INDEPENDENT SCIENCE ALONGSIDE THEOLOGY — and its task is precisely defined: SHARIA IS REGARDED NOT ONLY AS A LEGAL BUT ALSO AS A MORAL ORDER, AND IT IS THE TASK OF FIQH TO DISTINGUISH THE LEGAL NORMS FROM THE MORAL ONES. So it is not that law and morality are not distinguished at all — they are distinguished, but ONLY BY THE WORK OF THE JURIST, not already in the source itself. (3) LIKE HALAKHA, sharia too distinguishes NORMS GOVERNING THE COEXISTENCE OF PEOPLE WITH ONE ANOTHER from RULES GOVERNING MAN'S RELATION TO GOD. A practical consequence follows: NON-MUSLIMS living in countries where sharia applies MUST OBSERVE ONLY THE FIRST GROUP. BY CONTRAST, SHARIA DOES NOT KNOW THE DIVISION OF LAW INTO PRIVATE AND PUBLIC — and this is exactly the case where a European category does not fit a foreign order. THE EVALUATION OF CONDUCT has five degrees, beginning with WAJIB (obligatory) and HALAL (not forbidden, but not obligatory either).

cards.q: What is the task of fiqh in relation to sharia?
cards.a: FIQH is the LEGAL SCIENCE that established itself as an INDEPENDENT SCIENCE ALONGSIDE THEOLOGY. Because SHARIA IS REGARDED NOT ONLY AS A LEGAL BUT ALSO AS A MORAL ORDER, it is THE TASK OF FIQH TO DISTINGUISH THE LEGAL NORMS FROM THE MORAL ONES. Law and morality are therefore distinguished — but ONLY BY THE WORK OF THE JURIST, not already in the source.
cards.topic: Ancient Legal Cultures; History of Islamic Law

cards.q: Which division does sharia know and which does it not?
cards.a: It KNOWS the division into NORMS GOVERNING THE COEXISTENCE OF PEOPLE and RULES GOVERNING MAN'S RELATION TO GOD — which is why NON-MUSLIMS living under sharia must observe ONLY THE FIRST GROUP. It DOES NOT KNOW the division of law into PRIVATE AND PUBLIC — exactly the case where a European category does not fit a foreign order.

slides.title: The four Sunni schools and their character
slides.text: The exercise class gives for each school both its character and where it prevails today — and that is exactly what makes an answer concrete. MUHAMMAD IBN IDRIS AL-SHAFI'I is the founder of the SHAFI'I SCHOOL, which the exercise describes as the MIDDLE WAY BETWEEN THE HANAFI (very liberal, for example in Bosnia) AND THE CONSERVATIVE MALIKI; it prevails in MALAYSIA, SOMALIA and elsewhere. It proceeds from tradition but STRESSES THE IMPORTANCE OF THE CONSENSUS OF THE JURISTS. THE OTHERS: the HANAFI (Bosnia, for example); the MALIKI, where TRADITION AND CUSTOM PREDOMINATE (sub-Saharan Africa); the HANBALI, which takes the QUR'AN AS THE SOLE SOURCE OF LAW (Saudi Arabia). THE SOURCES ACCORDING TO THE EXERCISE: the QUR'AN is the holy book of Islam, the FIRST AND FUNDAMENTAL SOURCE of the provisions of sharia. The SUNNA is the NORMATIVE PRACTICE OF THE PROPHET; it too is of DIVINE ORIGIN, but it STANDS BEHIND THE QUR'AN — and the exercise adds a fine distinction worth remembering: THE SUNNA IS TRUE IN CONTENT BUT NOT IN WORDING. That is: what the Prophet taught holds; exactly how he said it has not been preserved verbatim. IJMA is the consensus of the scholars; among the Shiites the NORMATIVE PRACTICE OF THE IMAMS is added. And the RULE OF PRIORITY that the exercise draws from al-Shafi'i: IF A CONFLICT ARISES BETWEEN TWO SUNNAS, THE ONE CLOSER TO THE QUR'AN APPLIES.

cards.q: Characterize the four Sunni schools and say where they prevail.
cards.a: SHAFI'I — the MIDDLE WAY between Hanafi and Maliki, stressing the CONSENSUS OF THE JURISTS (Malaysia, Somalia). HANAFI — VERY LIBERAL (Bosnia). MALIKI — CONSERVATIVE, with TRADITION AND CUSTOM predominating (sub-Saharan Africa). HANBALI — the QUR'AN AS THE SOLE SOURCE (Saudi Arabia).
cards.topic: Ancient Legal Cultures; History of Islamic Law

cards.q: What is the relation of the Qur'an and the Sunna, and what rule of priority follows?
cards.a: The QUR'AN is the FIRST AND FUNDAMENTAL SOURCE. The SUNNA is likewise of DIVINE ORIGIN but STANDS BEHIND THE QUR'AN — and it is TRUE IN CONTENT BUT NOT IN WORDING (what the Prophet taught holds; exactly how he said it was not preserved verbatim). The rule of priority: IF A CONFLICT ARISES BETWEEN TWO SUNNAS, THE ONE CLOSER TO THE QUR'AN APPLIES.
